answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a stake-bonded reputation trellis: every identity must lock a refundable deposit that grows with each completed job, like ivory accumulating layer by layer, and the deposit is slashed if the agent cheats. A newcomer starts at the bottom of the spiral, able to take only tiny jobs until its deposit and history grow. An attacker who spawns a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand growing deposits and do real work for each, so the cost of faking scales linearly while the profit from one fraud stays flat.
